reasoning: UAV-borne CNN weed detection in line crops using unsupervised data labeling, segmenting crop rows and inter-row weeds; abstract describes pixel-level crop/weed segmentation and reports segmentation accuracy gaps, satisfying INC-01 and INC-02.

Fully-convolutional semantic-labeling CNN (with CRF refinement) maps weeds in high-resolution UAV rice-field imagery, reporting mean IoU 0.7751, overall accuracy 0.9445 and Kappa 0.9128 - a genuine UAV crop/weed pixel segmentation benchmark with quantitative metrics.

FCN performs weed mapping on UAV RGB rice-field imagery with overall accuracy 0.935 and weed-recognition accuracy 0.883, satisfying UAV DL crop/weed segmentation with pixel-level metrics (INC-01/INC-02).

FCN-4s performs pixel-level weed mapping and prescription-map generation from UAV rice-field imagery, reporting overall accuracy 0.9196 and mean IoU 0.8473 - a UAV crop/weed pixel segmentation with quantitative metrics.

WeedMap performs crop/weed semantic segmentation on UAV multispectral orthomosaics with a DNN, reporting AUC metrics per class (e.g. crop 0.863, weed 0.782) vs a SegNet baseline - satisfies UAV DL crop/weed segmentation with quantitative metrics.

Though the abstract reports only 'high classification accuracy', the full text confirms quantitative F1 scores (~0.85 with two channels at 50% labeled data) for pixel-wise crop/weed classification on the weedNet MAV (UAV) multispectral sugar-beet dataset, so INC-02 is satisfied.

This is a sorghum-panicle counting/phenotyping paper in the whole-plant counting gray zone; although it reports segmentation IoU (mean IoU 87%, per-class IoU), its primary contribution and headline metric are panicle count detection accuracy (94%) and count correlation, i.e. COUNTING rather than crop/weed discrimination.

DeepCount quantifies (counts) wheat spikes using SLIC+CNN on digital imagery taken in the field / from a ground-based Field Scanalyzer gantry - not UAV-borne aerial imagery (EXC-01) - and its primary purpose is wheat-ear counting in the whole-plant counting gray zone (COUNTING alone = out), reporting count metrics (rRMSE ~15%, R2 0.72) rather than a crop/weed segmentation benchmark.

A lightweight semantic-segmentation network maps weeds onboard a UAV, reporting 80.9% accuracy and 4.5 FPS on a Jetson TX2 with FP16 quantization - a direct match for UAV DL weed segmentation (INC-01/INC-02) plus on-device edge inference performance (INC-03).

Encoder-decoder CNNs perform pixel-wise crop/weed classification on ground and aerial images, including a third CNN specifically designed for small-UAV setups, on multiple public datasets with quantitative results; UAV-capable DL crop/weed pixel segmentation satisfying INC-01/INC-02.

This is vine/mildew disease detection in vineyard imagery - the fruit/orchard and disease-classification domain explicitly excluded by EXC-03 - rather than arable crop/weed segmentation; although it is a UAV FCN pixel-segmentation study with >92% detection, the target crop (grapevine) and disease task put it out of scope.

This is a pure UAV-platform/hardware design paper (amphibious drone, CATIA design, thrust/payload calculations, Arduino control) for sowing seed balls; it contains no deep-learning crop/weed segmentation and no quantitative segmentation metric, so it fails INC-01/INC-02.

A book chapter describing a UAV-based hyperspectral imaging sensor system for precision agriculture and forest management; it is secondary/technical literature describing sensor specs and image processing with no primary deep-learning crop/weed segmentation benchmark and no quantitative segmentation results.

This is a plant counting-and-sizing paper for potato and lettuce in the whole-plant counting gray zone (COUNTING alone = out); although it uses Mask R-CNN instance segmentation and reports mask-based mAP (0.418 potato, 0.660 lettuce), its stated objective is individual-plant counting/sizing rather than crop/weed discrimination, so it is a boundary case flagged out.

Mask R-CNN performs weed instance segmentation on aerial sugarcane imagery, reporting AP50 65.5% and F1 0.752 with ResNet-101 pre-trained COCO - genuine UAV (aerial) crop/weed pixel segmentation with quantitative mask metrics (INC-01/INC-02).

This is a secondary-literature book chapter on UAV-based precision agriculture (satellite-vs-drone sensing, vegetation indices, crop modelling) with no primary deep-learning segmentation benchmark and no quantitative crop/weed segmentation results, so it violates EXC-05 and EXC-06.

EDANet (a semantic-segmentation network) assesses rice lodging from UAV RGB imagery with edge computing, reporting 99.25% lodging-identification accuracy and edge-deployment scouting; rice is an arable crop and it reports a quantitative pixel-level accuracy metric (INC-01/INC-02) plus edge-computing context, so it is in scope despite the scouting focus.

UAV (DJI Matrice 100) crop classification via SegNet semantic segmentation with edge computing (ASUS Tinker Board, 4G offload), reporting 89% segmentation accuracy and ~0.7s inference - agricultural crop segmentation meeting INC-01/INC-02 with on-device latency (INC-03).

FCN-AlexNet and SegNet semantic segmentation of rice lodging in multi-date UAV visible imagery with vegetation indices, reporting F1 scores of 0.80 and 0.79 - a UAV crop-stress pixel-segmentation with quantitative metrics.

SemiWeedNet is a DNN-based semi-supervised semantic-segmentation method for crop/weed against complex backgrounds, reporting mIoU metrics (89.01% on the Bonn crop/weed dataset) consistent with INC-01/INC-02; however the evaluation uses ground-level Bonn/Stuttgart robot-field datasets rather than explicit UAV imagery, making the UAV-borne criterion ambiguous though not clearly excluded.

U-Net object segmentation is applied to the Aerial Semantic Segmentation Drone Dataset, which depicts urban scenes (houses, cars, persons, buildings, etc.), not crop/weed arable agronomy; although it reports 92-95% segmentation accuracy, the task domain is urban/infrastructure, so it violates EXC-03.

AgriSegNet performs UAV-acquired multiscale-attention semantic segmentation of farmland anomalies (including weed clusters, standing water) on the Agriculture-vision benchmark for precision agriculture, reporting quantitative segmentation results - UAV DL agricultural crop/anomaly pixel-segmentation in scope.

MAENet multiple-attention encoder-decoder performs farmland semantic segmentation on three self-made UAV image datasets, reporting MIoU 93.74% and Kappa 96.74% vs other methods - UAV agricultural crop/farmland pixel-level segmentation with quantitative metrics.

An improved OCRNet semantic-segmentation method identifies zucchini intercropped with sunflower in UAV visible images, reporting mIoU and intercropping IoU vs PSPNet/DeepLabV3+/DNLNet - arable crop pixel-level segmentation with quantitative metrics.

MobileNetV2-UNet and FFB-BiSeNetV2 semantic-segmentation models identify rice weeds from UAV low-altitude imagery, reporting pixel accuracy 93.09% / mIoU 80.28% and deployed on a Jetson AGX Xavier with TensorRT at 40-45 FPS - UAV weed segmentation with quantitative metrics AND on-device edge FPS (INC-01/02/03).

U-Net crop segmentation/classification from UAV multispectral imagery (wheat, cotton, maize, grass, soil classes) reports 83.35% accuracy and analyses NDVI/EVI/texture for semantic segmentation - agricultural crop pixel-level segmentation meeting INC-01/INC-02.

This is an adaptive UAV path-planning/robotics paper whose contribution is an altitude-vs-accuracy model and online trajectory replanning; crop/weed segmentation (ERFNet) is used only as the perception tool, and the reported mIoU (~0.5) is an evaluation of planning strategies, not a primary segmentation benchmark, so it is path-planning-only without a retrievable segmentation benchmark.

A lightweight Mobile U-Net extracts wheat-lodging regions from UAV RGB+DSM/ExG imagery, reporting 88.99% overall segmentation accuracy and lightweight model/fast-processing properties - arable crop pixel-segmentation with quantitative metrics (INC-01/INC-02, plus efficiency signal toward INC-03).
